probe.rationale: Time domain must match the reference values. This shifts HRV_MedianNN from 690.0 to 701.0 (about 1.6% change), which is far outside the stated relative tolerance, while all other cells, identities and empty-field pattern are preserved.
probe.script:
"""Wrong solution: shift a time-domain HRV metric value.

Sets HRV_MedianNN to a value +11ms from the reference, which is a
plausible alternative median NN interval but far outside the stated
1e-6 relative tolerance.
"""
import csv
from pathlib import Path

FILENAME = "hrv_indices.csv"


def main():
    p = Path(FILENAME)
    with p.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        rows = list(csv.reader(fh))
    assert len(rows) == 2
    header, values = rows
    assert len(header) == 95
    assert len(values) == 95
    i = header.index("HRV_MedianNN")
    old = float(values[i])
    values[i] = repr(old + 11.0)
    assert abs(float(values[i]) - old) > 1e-6 * abs(old) + 1e-9
    tmp = p.with_suffix(".csv.tmp")
    with tmp.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.writer(fh, lineterminator="\n")
        w.writerow(header)
        w.writerow(values)
    tmp.replace(p)
    print("mutated HRV_MedianNN", old, "->", values[i])

probe.name: valid-reencode-precision
probe.rationale: Public rule states text formatting is free and only parsed finite values are compared within tolerance. This probe reformats every finite value with a different decimal encoding (%.18g) that parses back to the exact same double and leaves all mandatory emptiness intact, testing that the implementation honors formatting freedom without rounding to a different value.
probe.script:
"""Valid representation control: different digit encoding of equal values.

Re-encodes all finite values using %.18g, which round-trips to the
exact same double, while leaving the five mandatory empty fields
(HRV_SDANN2, HRV_SDNNI2, HRV_SDANN5, HRV_SDNNI5, HRV_ULF) intact.
"""
import csv
from pathlib import Path

FILENAME = "hrv_indices.csv"


def main():
    p = Path(FILENAME)
    with p.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        rows = list(csv.reader(fh))
    assert len(rows) == 2
    header, values = rows
    assert len(header) == 95 and len(values) == 95
    out = []
    for x in values:
        if x == "":
            out.append("")
        else:
            out.append("%.18g" % float(x))
    for a, b in zip(values, out):
        if a == "":
            assert b == ""
        else:
            assert float(a) == float(b)  # exact same double
    tmp = p.with_suffix(".csv.tmp")
    with tmp.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.writer(fh, lineterminator="\n")
        w.writerow(header)
        w.writerow(out)
    tmp.replace(p)
    print("re-encoded all finite values with %.18g")


main()
